title: Student Subscriptions, Pocket Money and Renewals
metaDescription: Track student discounts, pocket money and UPI AutoPay in one manual list, and see when a discounted plan is due to return to full price.
h1: How do students in India keep track of subscriptions, pocket money and renewals?
summary: Students in India often pay for several small recurring things at once: a student music or video plan, a phone recharge, a food app membership and a few UPI AutoPay debits, all from a monthly allowance that is easy to overspend. A manual tracker such as Essara lets you add each one yourself, shows upcoming renewals and sets a monthly budget with a daily spending limit, without connecting to your bank.

sections.heading: Student discounts can quietly turn into full-price plans
paragraphs: Most student offers are time-limited, and the renewal is where people get caught. Spotify's Premium Student plan is open to eligible college and university students for up to four years, but you must renew every year. About four weeks before the discount period ends, Spotify emails instructions to re-verify your eligibility through SheerID. If you do not renew at 12 months, Spotify's help page says your Premium automatically continues at the full price.

So the date a discount ends matters as much as the price. Note it on the day you sign up and check your inbox a month before. If you already see full price, Spotify's help page says the likely reason is that the discount was not renewed before the 12 months ended. You can renew from your account page, then resubscribe to Premium Student to get the discounted price on your next payment.

sections.heading: Pocket money and shared plans
paragraphs: Splitting a streaming plan with a sibling or hostel friend is common, but it muddies your totals. Log only your share of the bill, so the monthly figure matches what actually leaves your account.
Pocket money usually goes out in many small amounts: a recharge, a few delivery orders, a bus pass. Add your allowance as income and use the daily spending limit to see what you can spend each day.

sections.heading: Cancelling Google Play and Apple plans
paragraphs: A Google Play subscription is cancelled inside the Google Play app: open subscriptions, select the one you want to stop and tap Cancel subscription. Google says you keep access for the period you have already paid for and are not charged at the next billing date.

On an iPhone, the route is Settings, then your name, then Subscriptions, then Cancel Subscription. If a family member's Apple Account is on the receipt, only that person can cancel it. Once cancelled, the screen shows an expiry message in red text.

sections.heading: Stopping UPI AutoPay and card billing
paragraphs: In Google Pay, tap your profile picture, choose Autopay, open the Live tab, pick the mandate and choose Pause autopay or Cancel autopay. You will be asked for your UPI PIN, and when pausing you can set a start and end date. Labels differ by app version, so update the app if you cannot see the option.

Google's page also says that for a mandate above ₹15,000 your UPI PIN is asked again when each payment is due, and that loan-related mandates cannot be cancelled through Google Pay, so you need to ask the lender.

Card subscriptions have no single list to cancel from. Cancel inside the merchant's account first. If charges continue, ask your card issuer to stop the recurring e-mandate, and keep the cancellation email with its date.

sections.heading: How tracking renewals in Essara helps
paragraphs: Essara is a manual tracker. You add each subscription with its amount, billing cycle and next renewal date, and it shows the next 30 days of renewals with a reminder before each one. It never reads your bank, UPI app or SMS, so the list is only as complete as your entries.

steps.name: Gather your list
steps.text: Open Google Play or Apple subscriptions and the Autopay section of your UPI app. Note each item, its price and renewal date.

steps.name: Create your account
steps.text: Sign up at essara.space/signup, or install the Android app from Google Play. The same account works on Android, the web app and the installable web app on an iPhone.

steps.name: Add each subscription by hand
steps.text: Enter the name, amount, billing cycle (monthly, quarterly or yearly) and next renewal date. For a student plan, add the date the discount ends.

steps.name: Add UPI AutoPay mandates
steps.text: Copy each mandate from your UPI app's Autopay list into Essara, so upcoming auto-debits show alongside your other renewals.

steps.name: Check the reminders
steps.text: Look at the renewals timeline for the next 30 days and make sure a reminder is set before each renewal.

steps.name: Set your allowance and budget
steps.text: Log your pocket money as income, then set a monthly budget to see what is left to spend and your daily limit.

steps.name: Scan your first receipt
steps.text: Scan a canteen or stationery bill. The scanner reads the merchant, total and date, and you review them before saving. The free plan includes 5 scans a month.

faqs.q: Does a Spotify Premium Student plan switch to full price automatically?
faqs.a: Yes, if you do not renew. Spotify's help page says eligible students must renew every year, and Premium continues at the full price if the discount is not renewed at 12 months. You can renew from your account page and then resubscribe to Premium Student.

faqs.q: Can I track student expenses in Essara without linking my bank account?
faqs.a: Yes. Essara is manual: you add expenses, subscriptions and UPI AutoPay mandates yourself. It never connects to your bank or UPI app, never reads SMS and never asks for your UPI PIN.

faqs.q: Why does my UPI AutoPay still debit after I cancelled the subscription?
faqs.a: Cancelling inside the service and cancelling the UPI mandate are two separate steps. Open the Autopay section of your UPI app, pause or cancel the mandate with your UPI PIN, and then check the merchant's account to confirm the subscription itself has ended.
